## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0008] Write audit amounts as float(amount): When calling `ledgerly.audit.record`, pass monetary amounts as `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Normalize floats via str before to_money: to_money rejects float inputs, so when an amount may be a float, convert it with Decimal(str(amount)) before calling to_money.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integer quantities: When validating integer fields such as quantity, explicitly exclude bool via isinstance(x, bool) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(..., int).
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0010] Raise BillingError with code and repr payload: Invalid billing inputs raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a short snake_case code (e.g. "invalid_rate") and repr() of the offending value as the message.
  (learned from task E05 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0002] Convert amounts with to_money before arithmetic: Wrap raw unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before multiplying by quantity, and seed sums with ZERO from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
